name: Brunete
story: On 6 July 1937 the Republic launched its first great offensive west of Madrid, aiming to cut off the Nationalist troops besieging the capital and to relieve pressure on the northern front. Líster's 11th Division took Brunete by surprise on the first day, but the attack stalled on Nationalist strongpoints at Villanueva de la Cañada and Quijorna and in the July heat. From 18 July Varela's counter-offensive, backed by the Condor Legion, pushed back, and Brunete was retaken on 24 July. The village was flattened and rebuilt after the war by the Regiones Devastadas agency.
see: A post-war rebuilt town; the parish church on the Plaza Mayor still shows bullet and shrapnel impacts, and the cemetery marks the last phase of fighting.
plan: Free; park near the Plaza Mayor. Combine with Quijorna and Villanueva de la Cañada (15 minutes' drive).

boxes.text: Republican losses are given as anything from 10,000 to 25,000 killed and wounded; Nationalist losses about 7,000–17,000 depending on source.
